note: The five flags form different contracts and cannot be cut as one unused group. The launcher inserts --interactive and --headless internally, so zero operator-typed occurrences cannot establish dead code. --no-dashboard is a documented foreground and background mode with a Remote Control safety check in AGENTS.md and the CLI reference. --logs-root was used by the isolated 2026-09-29 native Muse acceptance to keep the test run separate from the shared daemon; that is observed post-snapshot use, not evidence of frozen-period frequency. The guardrails acknowledgement is launcher-injected, and removing it changes the daemon's accepted launch contract. Consolidate internal mode handling if equivalent tests prove it; preserve the documented operator flags and safety behavior. Any line saving must be measured after implementation. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

A search that finds no `.aiurconfig` on the research host cannot measure installed users who still have one. The documented behavior deliberately rejects a legacy file with an actionable migration error, while config discovery otherwise falls through to `~/.aiur/config`. Removing that guard risks silently running a different workflow for a user who expected the local legacy file to apply. The 134-line gross estimate is too small to justify a compatibility break without a measured installed population and an equivalent fail-closed detection path. Keep the migration guard or replace it with a smaller equivalent; test local and global discovery precedence. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

`executor-fast-forward` is an exceptional repair for a wake prefix already covered by another complete means. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` and the CLI reference specify owner-lease checks, exact-prefix acknowledgement and preservation of newer wakes. Zero normal invocations is expected for an emergency recovery command and does not prove the recovery path is redundant with `executor-wait`, which acknowledges only its own successful consumption. Keep the capability unless an equivalent bounded recovery route is designed and tested. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

Automatic claims and lease expiry do not replace all manual authority transitions. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` treats `executor-revoke` as an operator decision after roster evidence and expressly forbids an agent from revoking a live peer itself. `executor-release` permits immediate handoff instead of waiting for TTL; claim refusal makes ownership visible. The zero-use sample is not a safe reason to remove these incident controls. Preserve them behind explicit owner/authority checks, or design and prove an equivalent takeover contract before removing a verb. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The five commands combine an optional raw stream with persistent event-bus administration. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` says `executor-listen` is optional, not obsolete, and describes `executor-emit` plus binding management for general Executor coordination; the CLI reference defines validated topic patterns. The zero invocation window does not measure all external operators or incident use. Consolidate the admin surface if the same event authority, replay, scope validation and observable receipts survive; do not delete the entire group based on a normal-loop usage count. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The evidence does not support deleting the agent chat capability or booking an 8,500-line saving. Aiur's documented human-driven foreground mode opens a live chat pane; AGENTS.md makes real TUI chat interaction the manual acceptance path. The 2026-09-29 native Muse acceptance used that path to display a skill read, an allow-once approval, a scoped tool result and a delivered follow-up. The inherited usage sample counts mostly headless runs and has no retained pane recordings, but a missing recording is not evidence that foreground users do not use the pane. The existing bridge's private opencode SQLite dependency is a valid simplification target. A plain transcript-backed TUI can replace it only after feature parity for rendered tool/prose output, typed operator input, queued delivery, approval commands, pause/resume and restart is demonstrated in the real CLI/TUI. Count removed lines after the replacement exists and includes its tests; moving the TUI to another package is relocation, not deletion. This challenge was performed by the continuing researcher, not an independent reviewer.

The frozen delivery census shows an actual failed webhook deployment, not an unused or redundant capability. `website/docs-app/apis/github.md` documents verified-delivery gating: failed or absent deliveries keep full polling and short cache TTLs; a proven delivery widens selected reconciliation reads and retires stale cache entries. Removing ingress would delete that conditional product contract and its event latency/reconciliation path. The cited 5,721 accepted deliveries in the earlier period show a real population, while 3,524 later 502 responses show the current path needs operational diagnosis. No quota saving may be claimed during the failed period, and the proposed 5,120-line deletion is a gross estimate that omits replacement work. Keep the capability while deciding whether to repair the deployment or replace transport; test loss recovery, signature validation and measured read displacement before any cut. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.
